questions.question: What is the conditional expectation $E[X\mid B]$?
options: The probability that $X$ equals event $B$
The variance of $X$ before observing $B$
The expectation of $X$ given that $B$ occurred.
The largest possible value that $X$ takes inside $B$.

questions.question: What condition is required on the event $B$?
options: $B$ must be the whole sample space
$B$ must be independent of $X$

questions.question: What information does conditional expectation use?
options: Only the unconditional sample space
Only impossible outcomes
The information that the condition holds.
The variance, but not the distribution itself.

questions.question: What distribution is used to compute conditional expectation?
options: The uniform distribution only
The distribution before any condition, unchanged
The conditional distribution
The distribution of a constant variable only

questions.question: Can conditioning increase or decrease expected value?
options: Either can happen, depending on the information
It can only decrease, since information reduces uncertainty
It can only increase, since the condition removes low values
It always equals $E[X]$ by the law of total expectation

questions.question: Which is an example of conditional expectation?
options: The expected repair cost given that a machine failed
The probability that a machine fails given that it is old
The expected repair cost averaged over all machines
The repair cost actually paid for one failed machine

questions.question: If weekend demand has a different distribution from weekday demand, what does $E[\text{demand}\mid \text{weekend}]$ describe?
options: The unconditional expected demand averaged over all days only
The probability that a day is weekend
The variance of weekday demand
The expected demand after restricting to weekend days

questions.question: Why is $E[X\mid B]$ not defined in the usual event-conditioning way if $P(B)=0$?
options: The conditional probability model given $B$ is not defined
$E[X\mid B]$ would equal $E[X]$, so conditioning adds nothing
$E[X\mid B]$ would be zero, since $B$ never occurs in practice
$X$ and $B$ would be dependent, which conditioning does not allow

questions.question: In a mixture model, what can group-specific conditional means help compute?
options: The number of impossible outcomes
The support of a uniform distribution only
The exact value of every observation
The overall mean

questions.question: If $B$ means a machine failed, which quantity is more targeted to failure cases?
options: $E[\text{repair cost}\mid B]$
$E[\text{repair cost}]$ without conditioning
$P(B^c)$ only
$\operatorname{Var}(B)$

questions.question: How does conditional expectation relate to conditional probability?
options: It averages the values of $X$ with weights $P(B\mid X=x)$
It equals $E[X\mathbf 1_B]$, without dividing by $P(B)$
It averages using probabilities updated by the condition
It applies only when $X$ is independent of the conditioning event

questions.question: What does the law of total expectation do?
options: It adds conditional expectations over a partition, without weights
It averages conditional expectations over any overlapping events
It combines conditional probabilities into an event's probability
It combines conditional expectations across a partition

questions.question: Why can $E[X\mid B]$ differ from $E[X]$?
options: $E[X\mid B]$ is $E[X]$ divided by $P(B)$, so it is always larger
$E[X\mid B]$ differs from $E[X]$ only when $X$ and $B$ are independent
Conditioning on $B$ changes the value of $X$ on each outcome
$B$ may select outcomes with a different distribution of $X$

questions.question: A machine has expected repair cost $20$ overall but $80$ given failure. What does the difference reflect?
options: Conditioning on failure changes the relevant distribution of costs
Conditional means are always larger than the unconditional mean
Repair cost and the failure event are independent of each other
Conditioning on failure removes all randomness from the repair cost

questions.question: If a partition has groups $G_1,G_2$ with probabilities $0.3,0.7$ and conditional means $10,20$, what is the overall mean?
If demand is higher on weekends, what is plausible?
options: $E[\text{demand}\mid \text{weekend}]=0$ necessarily
$P(\text{weekend})=0$ necessarily
$E[\text{demand}\mid \text{weekend}]>E[\text{demand}]$
Conditional demand cannot be averaged

questions.question: After observing partial information, the plain mean may no longer fit the situation. Which benefit does conditional expectation provide?
options: It removes all of the uncertainty from the problem
It avoids needing any probability model
It updates the average for observed information
It forces every group to share one mean

questions.question: Why does conditional expectation across mixture groups help with the overall mean?
options: The mean is the plain, unweighted average of the group means
The mean is group means weighted by the group variances
Each group mean must equal the overall mean
The mean is group means weighted by group probabilities

questions.question: Suppose $P(B)>0$ and $X$ is constant equal to $4$ on $B$. What is $E[X\mid B]$?
A solution uses $E[X\mid B]$ while stating $P(B)=0$. What is the issue?
options: The event-conditioning definition requires $P(B)>0$
Conditional expectation always exists for zero-probability events in this setup
The answer must be $E[X]$
The condition must be replaced by $B^c$ automatically
